title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chip Chop Before the Nvidia Swell
conditions.summary: Stocks slid across the board as traders sold chip and software names ahead of Nvidia's earnings, with the Dow down nearly 850 points. Nvidia then beat after the bell and rose in late trading.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53, and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.74% to 24,328.38.
The Dow lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, to 50,759.42; the Russell 2000 fell 1.50% to 2,701.87.
Traders sold chip and AI stocks ahead of Nvidia's first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO.
The Nasdaq was down about 2.1% at its worst, its lowest intraday level since April, before buyers trimmed losses in the last hour.
Decliners outnumbered advancers by nearly three to one on both the NYSE and Nasdaq at midday.
Enterprise software was hit hard, while consumer staples kept outperforming tech this year.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: October retail sales rose 0.2%, a bit better than the 0.1% expected; September was revised up to 0.8%.
The NAHB homebuilder index fell to 25 from 29, missing forecasts and hitting its lowest level since 2012.
October industrial production fell 0.4%, and import prices rose 1.1% for a second straight month.
St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem argued for another rate hike sooner rather than later.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased about 2 basis points to 5.10%, and the VIX jumped 11% to about 25.5.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: SLS (SELLAS Life Sciences): +156% — its Phase 3 AML vaccine trial met its main survival goal.
ENR (Energizer): +12.5% — fiscal Q4 adjusted profit rose 30% and it guided to higher free cash flow.
ACM (AECOM): +11.1% — record backlog of $28 billion and first fiscal 2027 outlook.
BILL (Bill Holdings): +13.2% — rallied with no clear news reported.
CRM (Salesforce): -9.6% — led a broad sell-off in enterprise software, with Intuit and ServiceNow down about 7%.
RCAT (Red Cat): -31.7% — pulled its full-year revenue target.
NXT (Nextpower): -12.1% — fell after its investor day despite a higher 2030 revenue goal.
JD (JD.com): -7.7% — third-quarter revenue grew only 3.5%.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Home Depot topped sales and profit estimates and named CFO Richard McPhail its next CEO, but the stock fell 2.4% on a soft implied fourth quarter.
Disney beat with adjusted EPS of $1.77 and revenue up 16%, and raised its dividend 33%, yet shares slipped 1.5%.
Klarna rose 4.8% after revenue grew 12%; Amer Sports gained 3.9% on raised guidance and a $1 billion buyback.
After the close, Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103%, and guided to about $130 billion next quarter; shares rose about 1.3% after hours.
fuboTV fell nearly 10% in after-hours trading.

sections.title: Business News
items: Aon closed its $17 billion purchase of insurance broker USI from KKR.
KKR completed its $5.7 billion take-private of medical device maker Integer Holdings.
UPS agreed to buy Australian healthcare courier Smartway Logistics, reportedly for about A$600 million.
The administration moved ahead with limits on Chinese data center equipment imports, jolting optical stocks.
JPMorgan named Bregje de Best as its next CFO, and BP launched tender offers for up to $6 billion of its debt.

sections.title: On Deck
items: October housing starts and building permits at 7:30 AM CT.
Minutes from the Fed's October meeting at 1:00 PM CT, watched for support for a December hike.
Before the open: Lowe's, Target and TJX report.
After the close: Palo Alto Networks reports.
Walmart reports Thursday morning.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November seventeenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down into the water, the tiki torches are lit, and we're paddling in from a choppy day. My co-anchor is curled up on his beach towel, sandy nose and all. Gus the wonder dog, give the Trade Wind surfers a sunset hello! Here's the final set. The S and P five hundred fell one point oh three percent to seven thousand three hundred forty. The Nasdaq slipped about three quarters of a percent to twenty-four thousand three hundred twenty-eight. The Dow lost almost eight hundred fifty points, or one point six four percent, to fifty thousand seven hundred fifty-nine. Small caps in the Russell two thousand fell one and a half percent. Traders bailed out of chip and A I stocks ahead of Nvidia's first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive. At the worst of it the Nasdaq was down about two percent, its lowest level since April. That was a gnarly drop, but buyers trimmed the losses in the last hour. Losers beat winners about three to one at midday, and enterprise software got rolled hard. Now the wind and weather. Retail sales rose two tenths of a percent in October, a touch better than expected. But the homebuilder mood index sank to twenty-five, its lowest since twenty twelve. Industrial production fell four tenths of a percent. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said he'd like another rate hike sooner. The ten-year Treasury yield eased about two basis points to five point one percent. The VIX fear gauge jumped eleven percent to about twenty-five and a half. Gold was flat, crude was flat, and bitcoin lost about one percent. Over in the lineup, SELLAS Life Sciences surged one hundred fifty-six percent after its leukemia vaccine trial hit its main goal. Energizer charged up twelve and a half percent on strong profits, and AECOM jumped eleven percent on a record backlog. Energizer really kept going and going all the way to the beach. Gus, that one's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! On the wipeout side, Salesforce fell almost ten percent, leading a software slide with Intuit and ServiceNow. Red Cat dropped thirty-two percent after pulling its revenue target. Kook move, that one. Tide chart time. Home Depot beat estimates and named a new chief executive, but slipped two percent. Disney beat and raised its dividend thirty-three percent, yet dipped one and a half percent. Then after the bell, the big Kahuna of chips reported. Nvidia posted revenue of one hundred fifteen point eight billion dollars, up one hundred three percent, and guided to about one hundred thirty billion next quarter. The stock rose about one percent after hours. Stoked to see that swell after a rough day. Beach talk: Aon closed its seventeen billion dollar deal for broker U S I. U P S agreed to buy an Australian healthcare courier. And J P Morgan named a new finance chief. Tomorrow's forecast: housing starts at seven thirty A M Central, and Fed minutes at one P M Central. Lowe's, Target and T J X report before the open, and Palo Alto Networks after the close. Soul surfers, don't let one choppy session shake you off your board. Catch Dawn Patrol in the morning while I wax the board for tomorrow. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
